items.text: Israel’s covenant with the Lord was like a marriage, meant for eternal commitment, shared experiences, and exclusive loyalty. Though they were not faithful, the Lord’s message was not rejection, but an invitation to return, promising, ‘I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness.’

The Lord declared through the prophet Hosea, ‘I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely.’ This same message is given to us today as we seek to live our covenants with love and devotion, offering us His boundless, unconditional love.

Joel testified that God ‘is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness.’ His words prompt us to ponder our own relationship with the Lord, inspiring us to consider how His faithfulness to us can encourage our faithfulness to Him.

Making a covenant with the Lord is like entering into a marriage. Failing to keep that covenant is like being unfaithful to a spouse. Yet, the Lord’s love and mercy are so great that He always invites us to return to Him.

In Hosea 14, the Lord makes beautiful promises to those who return to Him. The phrase 'love them freely' signifies His willingness to bless us abundantly, and the plant metaphors teach of the blessings of repentance and His enduring care.

The people in Hosea’s day offered sacrifices, but the Lord desired mercy and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. True devotion to God must be felt inwardly, encompassing a deep understanding and love for Him, not just outward acts.

When the people rend their garments as a sign of remorse, the Lord calls for them to rend their hearts. This means turning to God with genuine sorrow and sincere repentance, not just outward displays of grief or regret.

Joel prophesied that the Lord would ‘pour out [His] spirit upon all flesh.’ This outpouring of the Spirit is a profound blessing, essential for spiritual guidance, comfort, and for navigating the challenges of our day.

In our day, the prophecies of Joel are being fulfilled as the Lord pours out His Spirit. This divine influence is crucial for spiritual survival, providing direction, comfort, and constant connection to God.

President Russell M. Nelson taught, 'In coming days, it will not be possible to survive spiritually without the guiding, directing, comforting, and constant influence of the Holy Ghost.' Revelation is essential for our spiritual well-being.
